newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Record Australia sugar cane crush praised.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Record Australia sugar cane crush praised.

text.p: Australia's 28 raw sugar mills set an extraordinary achievement in crushing a record crop of 39.6 million tonnes of cane in 1996, Australian Sugar Milling Council general manager John Desmarchelier said on Thursday.
Queensland's record 1996 crop of 37.2 million tonnes was crushed in a shorter time than in 1995, the previous record crop year, he said in a statement.
Australian sugar millers had developed a capacity to transport and crush nearly two million tonnes of cane a week if growers could maintain supply, he said.
In the 1996 season, mills crushed more than 1.8 million tonnes a week on at least 10 occasions, with the best throughput 1.92 million tonnes in the week ended September 21.
In the 1995 season, mills crushed more than 1.8 million tonnes a week on three occasions.

The 1996 achievement reflected substantial capital investment in recent years, in crushing, processing and transport infrastructure. There had also been significant investment by growers in expansion, with the assigned area in Queensland now more than 500,000 hectares, he said.
Since 1970 the tonnage of cane crushed had increased by more than two and a half times, while the number of Queensland mills had declined to 25 from 31.

Australia's grower organisation CANEGROWERS reported on Wednesday that Australia's 1996 season sugar crush had risen to 39.543 million tonnes from 37.390 million the year before. Sugar content had also risen, to 13.50 percent from 13.12 percent.
